I have worked this land in Quzhou for 50 years, and at 70 I know every mu of my 30 mu farm by heart. It is just my wife and me at home now—our family works off-farm in the city and sends money back, but they cannot help in the fields. Because there are only two of us and my back is not what it used to be, I hire machines for the heavy work: rotary tilling before wheat, combine harvesting for both crops, and no-till planting for maize. I have a well, and that well is my insurance when the sky does not give us enough rain.

This year I will keep my wheat-maize rotation on all 30 mu. For winter wheat, I will rotary till after the maize stubble is chopped and spread, then sow the improved wheat variety I have trusted for years—about 30 jin per mu. I put down compound fertilizer as a base before sowing, and top-dress with urea at greening and jointing. Wheat needs water at the critical times, so I will irrigate three times from my well: once before winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once during grain filling. If I miss the jointing water, the heads will be small and the yield will drop. I spray herbicide after the wheat regreens, and I watch closely for aphids and rust; if they show up, I spray insecticide and fungicide without delay. A steady wheat crop should give me around 550 kg per mu.

For summer maize, the days after wheat harvest in early June are the busiest of my year. I plant hybrid maize seed the same day we thresh the wheat—there is no time to lose before the season turns. I use no-tillage planting because it saves time, keeps the soil moisture, and the maize roots take hold just fine. I put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, then side-dress nitrogen when the plants reach knee height. I irrigate twice: at the big trumpet stage and again during grain filling if the rain does not come. I apply herbicide before emergence and keep an eye out for corn borers. I expect about 600 kg per mu from the maize.

I do not gamble on new methods or untested seeds anymore. At my age, a stable harvest that I can manage with my own well and hired machines is worth more than chasing a few extra jin.
